Subject: POC trial conductor: stakeholder lattice, success metrics & next steps

Hi Lauren / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo with us today. Per our call, I wanted to capture a compact trial "conductor" blueprint we can agree on quickly so the trial is measurable and stays on schedule. High level below; please flag anything missing.

Goal: Validate inference latency and total cost at 250 concurrent users on your core clinical-search flow; measure average 95th-percentile latency and embedding recall over the sample dataset.

Proposed success criteria (engineering + product):
- Latency: 95th pct < 350ms for 80% of requests during simulated weekday peak.
- Cost: token cost below your budget threshold (TBD) at target concurrency with suggested batching/quantization.
- Quality: embedding recall >= 92% on the curated evaluation prompts.
- Ops: No production-impacting errors during 72-hour soak.

Evaluation plan & timeline (suggested):
- Week 0 (this week): Align owners & network/security checklist.
- Week 1: Private trial environment provisioned (VPC peering or private link) + initial smoke tests.
- Week 2: Run scripted traffic profile (peak/steady) + run evaluation prompt set.
- Week 3: Results review, tuning, acceptance or propose remediation run.

Ownership / RACI (proposed lattice):
- Trial leader (conductor): Michael Grant (Redwood) — scheduling, runbook, results consolidation.
- Infra & network: Kimberly Park (Redwood) — provisioning, peering, firewall rules, performance knobs.
- App integration & replay scripts: Priyom Das (Redwood) — sample client, load profiles, KV cache guidance.
- Security / compliance liaison: Rishi Malhotra (Redwood) — questionnaire responses, data handling, audit logs.
- Aurora on-call / approver: Lauren Briggs — product acceptance & scheduling; Tom Eyre — infrastructure sign-off; Priya Natarajan — procurement/commercial.

Immediate asks for you (Lauren/Tom):
1) Confirm the four owners above or substitute the Aurora names for infra/security/procurement.
2) Share the security questionnaire your team prefers (if you have one) — we can start populating answers.
3) Quick sync: 30 minutes to lock timeline tomorrow (I have 10:00–11:30am PT).

Attachments: I do not have a SOW yet; I can drop a light SOW template once we lock timing (to speed procurement).

If that looks right, I'll circulate a one-pager runbook and an invite for the alignment call.

—
Michael Grant

- Firewall / IP ranges: we'll provide a minimal allowlist of outbound IPs and the ephemeral port ranges we use for batching; expect a short inbound rule for the healthcheck endpoint.
- Observability: we'll add a per-route latency dashboard and a token-level cost breakdown to the shared runbook.
- 99th percentile: agree we should capture 99th spike window during the 72-hour soak; we'll include both 95th and 99th in the report.

I'll draft a compact RACI table and upload the runbook to a shared Drive folder — link will follow. For the security questionnaire, assigning Rishi to populate sections 3–5 as noted.
